reserve_hypotheses.hypothesis: Deleting redundant materialized/generic aggregate structure can reduce kernel replay cost without changing mathematical semantics.
A universally fixed structural parameter may be specialized away when its value is proved from the input generator rather than inferred from scored inputs.
When a kernel-reduced producer constructs an intermediate list only for an immediate consumer, a proved fused traversal may reduce instructions.
Generated dynamic state can be cheaper than replaying naive recursive semantics when the state is produced inside measured computation.
For hot kernel-reduction paths, replacing x^2 with x*x may reduce definitional reduction overhead while preserving semantics.
When multiplying by an exact power of two in a hot kernel path, a proved shift representation may reduce replay cost.
Explicit structural recursion may reduce kernel cost relative to generic well-founded least-factor reduction.
